protocol.description:
This protocol informs the river-window-management-v1 window manager when a window requests activation, for example through xdg-activation-v1.
It is not part of upstream river.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: hrwm_activation_v1
interface.description:
This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.
Events are only sent to the client that is bound to the river_window_manager_v1 global.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the object and that it may be safely destroyed.

event.name: activation_requested
event.description:
The window has requested to be activated, perhaps to get the user's attention.
The xdg-activation-v1 protocol for example allows windows to request activation, and X11 windows may do so by sending a _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW message, setting _NET_WM_STATE_DEMANDS_ATTENTION or setting the ICCCM urgency hint.
The window manager is free to ignore this request, focus the window, mark the window as urgent, or do whatever else it chooses.
This event is sent as part of the window state preceding a river_window_manager_v1.manage_start event and will be followed by that manage_start event.
